findings.claim: The pre-apply check now runs one way, GCS to SeaweedFS, with a rule for objects an app deleted after its restore. The outcome check runs two ways after the backup run, when sync has made GCS match SeaweedFS.

The outcome is now scoped to S3 clients other than `minio` itself, and keeps Prometheus's scrape. The only other job that names MinIO's endpoint, `memex.hcl`, is commented out in `deployments/applications/services.tf`.

The pre-apply one-way check `rclone check gcs:.../minio/<b>/ seaweedfs:<b> --one-way` also reports objects that exist on both sides but differ in size or hash. Consumers overwrite keys after their restore: the registry rewrites `_manifests/tags/<tag>/current/link` on every push of an existing tag such as `latest`, and OpenViking can rewrite its own files in place. Those show as differences, not as missing objects. The plan's rule explains only missing objects ("An object an app deleted ... shows as missing ... stop if one cannot be explained"), so an operator following it stops on the first retag and the backup switch never happens. This is the same gate-fails-by-design problem as p1. Fix: extend the rule to objects changed after the restore. For each one, record the app that wrote it and check that SeaweedFS's modtime is later than the restore. `rclone check` already lists the two kinds apart (`--missing-on-dst` and `--differ` write them to separate files).
